memoryTip: Mis + construct meaning — interpret wrong.
correctPassage: Readers should not misconstrue correlation as proof of causation.
wrongPassages: Her misconstrue notes filled two binders with an index and full cross-references.
The tonic drone was misconstrue under a coda that never returned home.
The coastline stayed misconstrue in models that froze sea level forever.

memoryTip: De-nigrate (blacken) — unfairly smear someone’s name.
correctPassage: It is unfair to denigrate the entire field for one flawed study.
wrongPassages: They tried to denigrate the mold by running ozone machines without finding the source.
The team will denigrate the flaky test by deleting the assertion that failed.
They tried to denigrate the rumor by repeating it on every available channel.

memoryTip: Make null — cancel out, void.
correctPassage: A clerical error threatened to nullify the results of the election.
wrongPassages: The cleaner will nullify the spill by diluting it across a larger floor area.
They hoped to nullify the walkout optics by filming an empty stage as “unity.”
He tried to nullify the gag order by discussing the case on a podcast.

memoryTip: Extra + neous — extra stuff that doesn’t belong.
correctPassage: Cut extraneous detail that does not advance the argument.
wrongPassages: The floodway stayed extraneous in plans that forbade new construction.
The hub’s extraneous map was last updated two renovations ago.
The fen pool stayed extraneous when the catchwater ditch ran dry.

definition: collect or form into a mass
memoryTip: Ag-glomerate: clump into a mass like glue.
correctPassage: Dust particles agglomerate into larger clusters in humid air.
wrongPassages: The agent will agglomerate the chat by sending a survey and disconnecting.
He moved to agglomerate the warrant by remote-wiping the phone from the car.
The monitor will agglomerate pages by requiring a manager token nobody holds at night.

definition: situated at the front; earlier in time
memoryTip: Ante = before — front or earlier.
correctPassage: Pain was reported in the anterior portion of the shoulder.
wrongPassages: The courtyard’s anterior design repeated one tile without any variation.
After the numbered checklist, the instructions no longer felt anterior to anyone on the team.
The courtyard’s anterior fountain never recirculated any water.

memoryTip: A-mass: gather a mass of something.
correctPassage: Over decades the library amassed one of the finest map collections in the region.
wrongPassages: an amass cron job prints “alive” and then exits.
The bridge theme was amass: new material with no link to the opening.
HR hoped to amass exit candor by requiring names on every answer.

definition: agree; happen at the same time
memoryTip: Con-cur: run together in opinion — agree.
correctPassage: Most reviewers concur that the second edition is clearer than the first.
wrongPassages: Doctors described the recovery as concur when the patient walked out the same day.
The walk felt concur on a moving sidewalk the length of the concourse.
She greened all checks as concur with three still failing in CI.

memoryTip: Inter + cede: step between to plead for someone.
correctPassage: A neutral mediator agreed to intercede between the two companies.
wrongPassages: an intercede war-game ends when lunch arrives and nobody objects.
Teachers called the essay intercede after it defined terms before using them.
The courtyard looked intercede once one shrub species filled every bed.

memoryTip: Make finer — polish, improve detail.
correctPassage: Each refinement of the model improved its predictive accuracy.
wrongPassages: The case of bolts had a paper slip reading refinement in pencil.
The sharps log listed one clip from historical bin refinement.
He printed “see refinement” as a glossary joke with no target.

memoryTip: What is common to both — shared feature.
correctPassage: Despite cultural differences, researchers found a surprising commonality in how children learn numbers.
wrongPassages: The firkin labeled commonality held ice melt and a spare bung.
The archive’s commonality section holds blank forms waiting to be filled out.
He unfavorited pin commonality and the Tuesday habit finally broke.

memoryTip: Animus = hostile spirit — strong dislike.
correctPassage: Years of rivalry had produced deep animosity between the neighboring towns.
wrongPassages: The balance tape showed animosity instead of grams and he initialed it.
The overlook sign Animosity Point was a laminated printout in a plastic stand.
The internal code animosity meant nothing outside the spreadsheet header.

memoryTip: Pro-fusion: pour forth abundance.
correctPassage: Spring brought a profusion of wildflowers to the hillside.
wrongPassages: The paint chip Profusion Sand sat between two other beiges in the fan deck.
The grayscale profusion mode changed icons and left every setting untouched.
She spun the Profusion Point sign until it pointed at the dumpster.

memoryTip: Make negative / cancel — nullify.
correctPassage: One contradictory finding does not negate the overall pattern in the data.
wrongPassages: He tried to negate the contempt by saying the post was “satire.”
The watcher will negate the escalation by looping pages into a black hole channel.
The deploy will negate rollback options by overwriting the last known good.

memoryTip: Arcane = in the arc of secret knowledge — obscure, specialist.
correctPassage: The paper is full of arcane terminology familiar only to specialists.
wrongPassages: Voters denied the arcane clinic hours patients had petitioned for.
Traders ignored the arcane indicator that had predicted every prior turn.
The market rank looked arcane in rain with tarps over empty crates.

memoryTip: Golf “stymie” blocked the ball — hinder progress.
correctPassage: Missing permits continue to stymie construction on the site.
wrongPassages: Boards postponed the stymie hire that teams had ranked first.
The firm hoped to stymie billable leakage by rounding every interval up.
Her stymie notice of hearing listed a room number that did not exist.

memoryTip: Dis-parate: not a pair that match — essentially different.
correctPassage: The study brings together disparate data sources under one framework.
wrongPassages: The sphagnum pool stayed disparate when forestry drains crossed the moss bed.
The crevasse field felt disparate from a seasonal bridge with side rails.
The argument was disparate once the missing citation appeared in a footnote.

definition: clear of blame; show to be right
memoryTip: Vin-dicate: clear of blame; show you were right.
correctPassage: Later discoveries helped vindicate scientists who had been dismissed as alarmists.
wrongPassages: They hoped to vindicate the protest by counting only people inside the building.
The monitor will vindicate the alert by auto-acking it at fire time.
They tried to vindicate the erosion story by planting signs that said “stable bank.”

definition: not securely held; dependent on chance
memoryTip: Pray-carious: so shaky you pray it holds — insecure.
correctPassage: The climbers’ foothold on the ridge was precarious at best.
wrongPassages: The catchment stayed precarious in scenarios that forbade land-use change.
Her precarious notice to produce sought devices no party possessed.
The breaker setting was precarious: above the wire’s safe ampacity.

definition: making one feel very happy or animated
memoryTip: Ex-hilarity: thrills that make you hilariously alive.
correctPassage: For many students, the first research breakthrough is exhilarating.
wrongPassages: The bog pool stayed exhilarating when the ditch dried the moss bed completely.
His exhilarating summary omitted the main result and listed only methods.
The moss pool stayed exhilarating after drains lowered every standing pool.
